Internal dataset of an AI assistant producing structured, step-by-step project plans.

- Data lives in `data/entries.dat` (one JSON object per line, fields: `prompt`, `response`).
- Add entries ONE AT A TIME with the CLI (direct edits to the data file will fail the

      echo '{"prompt": "...", "response": "..."}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py

- Before pushing, run `make check`.

final_entries.prompt: I want to plan a 10-day road trip through the Pacific Northwest next summer. Help me structure the itinerary.
final_entries.response:
Here is a structured 10-day Pacific Northwest road trip plan:

Days 1-2 (Seattle area): Day 1 - Arrive, explore Pike Place Market and Seattle Center. Day 2 - Visit the Space Needle and take a ferry to Bainbridge Island for coastal views.

Days 3-5 (Olympic Peninsula): Day 3 - Drive to Port Angeles, explore Hurricane Ridge. Day 4 - Hike in Hoh Rainforest (Hall of Mosses trail). Day 5 - Ruby Beach and Hole-in-the-Wall Rock at sunset.

Days 6-7 (Columbia River Gorge): Day 6 - Drive east, stop at Multnomah Falls and several waterfall viewpoints. Day 7 - Explore the Gorge vineyards and towns like Hood River.

Days 8-9 (Mount Rainier): Day 8 - Drive to Mount Rainier, hike Skyline Trail if Nisqually Parkway is open. Day 9 - Paradise area, wildflower meadows, and reflection lakes.

Day 10 (Return): Drive back to Seattle, optional stop at Snoqualmie Falls and Cascade Locks on the way.

Pro tip: Reserve campgrounds/lodging 3-6 months ahead and check for chain requirements if traveling Nov-April. Want a printable version or budget estimate?

final_entries.prompt: I'm organizing a charity 5K run for my local community in 3 months. What's a step-by-step plan to pull it off?
final_entries.response:
Here's a phased 12-week plan for your charity 5K:

Weeks 1-4 (Foundation & permits): Secure the route with city permits, set a fundraising goal, form a 5-person organizing committee, pick a date and register the event name.

Weeks 5-7 (Sponsorship + vendor outreach): Create a sponsor one-sheet (logo on t-shirt, booth space, etc.), approach 10-15 local businesses, confirm water/timing/medical providers, book a DJ or playlist.

Weeks 8-10 (Marketing + registration): Launch a registration page (Runsignup or Eventbrite), print flyers and post in community centers/groceries, start Instagram/Facebook event, begin weekly social posts counting down.

Weeks 11-12 (Final prep): Confirm all vendors for race day, order t-shirts and bibs, map out volunteer shifts (water stations, registration, cleanup), do a route walk with volunteers 3 days prior.

Race day checklist: Arrive 4 hours early, set up registration 2h before start, have a megaphone for announcements.

Want a volunteer role roster template?

final_entries.prompt: Help me plan a 4-week program to learn meal prepping and cook healthier meals from scratch.
final_entries.response:
Here's a structured 4-week meal prep learning plan:

Week 1 (Basics & kitchen setup): Inventory your kitchen, buy core tools (meal prep containers, sharp knife, cutting board), choose 3 simple recipes (one-protein, one-grain, one-veggie), do a focused grocery trip for Week 1 ingredients only.

Week 2 (Systems & batch cooking): Pick a 2-hour prep window (Sunday afternoon works for most), practice cooking proteins in bulk (chicken breast, tofu, beans), learn to chop 3-4 veggie types ahead, store everything labeled with dates.

Week 3 (Variety & flavor): Introduce 2 new recipes, experiment with 3 sauce/marinade formulas, start a meal rotation (Mon-Wed one recipe, Thu-Sat another), take photos to build your own recipe library.

Week 4 (Refinement & scaling): Time your prep sessions and cut by 20%, try freezing 3-4 meals for emergency backups, calculate your weekly food budget, assess what worked and what didn't.

Ongoing: Adjust portions weekly, swap proteins for dietary needs, aim for 80% prepped + 20% fresh.

Want a printable grocery checklist template?

final_entries.prompt: I need to upgrade my home network and set up a more secure Wi-Fi system. Help me plan the project.
final_entries.response:
Here's a structured home network upgrade plan:

Phase 1 - Assessment (Week 1): Map your home layout and dead zones, list all connected devices and their bandwidth needs (gaming, 4K streaming, video calls), check your current router's age and specs, decide if your ISP modem can be replaced.

Phase 2 - Equipment selection (Week 1-2): Choose a mesh Wi-Fi system if your home is over 1,500 sq ft, pick a router with Wi-Fi 6 if budget allows, buy a managed Gigabit switch if you have 10+ wired devices, order a UPS for network gear.

Phase 3 - Installation (Weekend project): Replace the ISP modem if applicable, set up the primary router/mesh node with a custom SSID and WPA3 password, place satellite nodes centrally, run Ethernet cables to key rooms if needed.

Phase 4 - Security hardening (Week 3): Change all default admin passwords, enable WPA3 encryption, set up a guest network for visitors, disable WPS and remote management, install firmware updates, consider a DNS filter for ad/malware blocking.

Phase 5 - Testing & documentation (Week 4): Speed test from multiple rooms, verify all devices reconnect properly, document your network diagram and passwords securely, set a calendar reminder for quarterly firmware checks.

Pro tip: Keep your old router boxed for 30 days in case you want to revert. Want specific product recommendations?

final_entries.prompt: I want to start a community garden in my neighborhood. Can you give me a plan for getting it off the ground in 6 months?
final_entries.response:
Here's a 6-month phased plan to launch a community garden:

Months 1-2 (Planning & partnerships): Form a 5-8 person steering committee, identify potential sites (vacant lots, schoolyards, parks), reach out to the city about land-use permits and liability insurance, draft a simple mission statement and bylaws.

Months 3-4 (Design & funding): Survey the land for sun exposure, soil quality, and water access, sketch plot layouts (individual plots, communal beds, compost area), apply for local grants or sponsorships, launch a neighborhood crowdfunding or donation drive.

Months 5 (Infrastructure build): Clear the site and test soil, bring in compost/topsoil where needed, build raised beds and a tool shed with volunteers, install a rain barrel or garden hose bib, set up signage and plot assignment boards.

Month 6 (Soft launch): Host a volunteer planting day, assign plots to the first 20-30 families, establish shared rules (organic-only, shared tool care, water schedule), plan a summer potluck to celebrate the opening.

Ongoing: Hold monthly meetings, rotate a garden coordinator role, start a seed library for the next season.

Want a plot application form template?
